mcqs.question: A spherical mirror forms an image with a magnification of -0.5. What does this indicate about the image?

options.A: Image is upright and half the size of the object
options.B: Image is inverted and half the size of the object
options.C: Image is upright and twice the size of the object
options.D: Image is inverted and twice the size of the object

mcqs.answer: Image is inverted and half the size of the object
mcqs.explanation: Magnification (m) = -v/u. A negative value means the image is inverted with respect to the object. The magnitude |m| = 0.5 shows the image height is half the object height. Hence the image is inverted and half the size.

mcqs.question: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror whose focal length is 15 cm. Using the Cartesian sign convention, what is the image distance?
mcqs.explanation: For a concave mirror, f = -15 cm and u = -30 cm. Mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u → 1/(-15) = 1/v + 1/(-30). Solving gives 1/v = -1/30, so v = -30 cm. The negative sign indicates a real image on the same side as the object.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly expresses the mirror formula for spherical mirrors using the Cartesian sign convention?
mcqs.explanation: The standard mirror formula, valid for both concave and convex mirrors when the Cartesian sign convention is applied, is 1/f = 1/v + 1/u. The signs of f, v, and u are taken care of by the convention, not by altering the formula.

mcqs.question: An object is placed 20 cm in front of a convex mirror whose focal length is +10 cm. Using the Cartesian sign convention, what is the image distance?
mcqs.explanation: For a convex mirror, f = +10 cm and u = -20 cm. Mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u → 1/10 = 1/v - 1/20. Solving gives 1/v = 1/10 + 1/20 = 3/20, so v = 20/3 ≈ +6.7 cm. The positive sign indicates a virtual image behind the mirror.

mcqs.question: A concave mirror has a focal length of 6 cm. An object is placed 12 cm in front of it. What is the position of the image?
mcqs.explanation: Here f = -6 cm, u = -12 cm. Using 1/f = 1/v + 1/u → 1/(-6) = 1/v + 1/(-12). Solving gives 1/v = -1/12, so v = -12 cm. The image is real and formed at the same distance as the object on the same side of the mirror.

mcqs.question: A concave mirror has a focal length of -15 cm. An object is placed 20 cm in front of the mirror. What is the magnification of the image produced?
mcqs.explanation: First find image distance: f = -15 cm, u = -20 cm. 1/(-15) = 1/v + 1/(-20) → 1/v = -1/15 + 1/20 = -1/60, so v = -60 cm. Magnification m = -v/u = -(-60)/(-20) = +3. Positive magnification indicates an upright, enlarged image (virtual) formed behind the mirror.

mcqs.question: Statement: "A magnification of -2 means the image formed by a spherical mirror is upright and twice the size of the object." Is this statement true or false?

options.C: Cannot be determined without knowing the mirror type
options.D: Both true and false depending on the sign convention used

mcqs.explanation: A negative magnification indicates that the image is inverted relative to the object. The magnitude (2) tells the size is twice that of the object, but the image is not upright. Therefore the statement is false.

mcqs.question: An object is placed 40 cm in front of a concave mirror whose focal length is 10 cm. Using the Cartesian sign convention, determine the image distance, the nature of the image, and its magnification.

options.A: Image at +13.33 cm, magnification +0.33, virtual upright
options.B: Image at -13.33 cm, magnification -0.33, real inverted
options.C: Image at -13.33 cm, magnification +0.33, virtual upright
options.D: Image at +13.33 cm, magnification -0.33, real inverted

mcqs.answer: Image at -13.33 cm, magnification -0.33, real inverted
mcqs.explanation: Given f = -10 cm, u = -40 cm. Mirror formula: 1/(-10) = 1/v + 1/(-40) → 1/v = -1/10 + 1/40 = -3/40, so v = -40/3 ≈ -13.33 cm (negative → real image on the same side as the object). Magnification m = -v/u = -(-13.33)/(-40) = -0.33, a negative value confirming the image is inverted and reduced in size. Option B correctly lists all three attributes.
